segments.text: Twenty Christmas gifts, from twelve dollars, sorted by who they're for: Mom, the home cook, the one who works from home, and the friend who says don't get me anything.
Quick note: prices move daily, so always check the link for today's price.
For Mom, and every woman who does it all.
segments.label: For Mom
segments.sub: And every woman who does it all

segments.name: Fuzzy faux-fur slippers
segments.text: Number one. Fuzzy faux-fur slippers, about sixteen dollars. Warm feet the second she walks in, and she'll wear them every evening. The catch? If she's between sizes, go up.
segments.catch: Between sizes? Go up.

segments.name: Candle warmer lamp
segments.text: Number two. A candle warmer lamp, about twenty dollars. The cozy glow of a candle, with no open flame to worry about. The catch? The candle isn't included, so check her jar fits.
segments.catch: Candle not included. Check the jar fits.

segments.name: Hommey silk eye mask
segments.text: Number three. A silk eye mask, about twenty-seven dollars. A small luxury she'd never buy for herself. The catch? It's hand-wash only.
segments.catch: Hand-wash only.

segments.name: Owala FreeSip 40 oz
segments.text: Number four. The Owala FreeSip, about thirty-five dollars. The bottle everyone's carrying this year, and she'll take it everywhere. The catch? The forty-ounce size won't fit every cup holder.
segments.catch: 40 oz won't fit every cup holder.

segments.name: Charlotte Tilbury mini set
segments.text: Number five. A Charlotte Tilbury mini set, about fifty-four dollars. A big-name gift that feels special to unwrap. The catch? The sets change every year, so check what's inside.
segments.catch: Sets change yearly. Check what's inside.

segments.text: For the one who feeds everyone.
segments.label: The home cook
segments.sub: For the one who feeds everyone

segments.name: Lodge cast iron skillet
segments.text: Number six. A Lodge cast iron skillet, about twenty dollars. The pan they'll cook with for decades, and maybe hand down. The catch? It's heavy, and it needs drying and a little oil after washing.
segments.catch: Heavy. Dry and oil it after washing.

segments.name: ThermoPop 2 thermometer
segments.text: Number seven. The ThermoPop two thermometer, about thirty-nine dollars. No more cutting into the roast to check it. The catch? It's instant-read, so it can't stay in the oven.
segments.catch: Instant-read. It can't stay in the oven.

segments.name: Instant Pot Duo, 6 qt
segments.text: Number eight. The Instant Pot Duo, about seventy dollars. Weeknight stews and rice, mostly hands-off. The catch? It takes counter space, and a little practice.
segments.catch: Needs counter space and practice.

segments.name: Lodge enameled Dutch oven
segments.text: Number nine. A Lodge enameled Dutch oven, about seventy dollars. The Sunday-stew pot that goes straight to the table. The catch? Enamel can chip if it's knocked, or heated empty.
segments.catch: Enamel can chip. Never heat it empty.
segments.q: lodge 6 quart enameled cast iron dutch oven

segments.name: Ninja Crispi Pro air fryer
segments.text: Number ten. The Ninja Crispi Pro air fryer, about a hundred and ninety-nine dollars. Cook, serve and store in one glass dish, so there's no basket to scrub. The catch? The glass dish is heavier than a basket.
segments.catch: The glass dish is heavy.
segments.q: ninja crispi pro 6 qt glass air fryer

segments.text: Still coming: a mug that keeps coffee warm through the longest call, and the twelve-dollar gift their dog will thank you for.
For the one who works from home.
segments.label: Home office
segments.sub: For the one who works from home

segments.name: Aluminum laptop stand
segments.text: Number eleven. An aluminum laptop stand, about thirty dollars. Their screen at eye level, every single workday. The catch? They'll need a separate keyboard and mouse.
segments.catch: They'll need a keyboard and mouse.

segments.name: 3-in-1 wireless charger
segments.text: Number twelve. A three-in-one wireless charger, about thirty-five dollars. One tidy spot for phone, earbuds and watch. The catch? Check it fits their phone and watch brand.
segments.catch: Check it fits their phone and watch.

segments.name: Ember Mug 2, 14 oz
segments.text: Number thirteen. The Ember Mug two, from about ninety dollars. Coffee still warm after the longest call. The catch? The battery is short off the coaster, and it's hand-wash only.
segments.catch: Short battery off the coaster.

segments.name: BenQ ScreenBar light
segments.text: Number fourteen. The BenQ ScreenBar, about a hundred and nine dollars. Soft light for late evenings, with no glare on the screen. The catch? It needs a monitor, not a laptop.
segments.catch: Needs a monitor, not a laptop.

segments.name: Logitech MX Master 4
segments.text: Number fifteen. The Logitech MX Master four, about a hundred and twenty dollars. The mouse people never go back from. The catch? It's big, and right-handed only.
segments.catch: Big and right-handed only.

segments.text: For the friend who says, don't get me anything.
segments.label: Everyone else
segments.sub: For the friend who says 'don't get me anything'

segments.name: KONG Classic dog toy
segments.text: Number sixteen. A KONG Classic, about twelve dollars. For the dog they love more than anyone. The catch? Match the size to the dog. Too small is a choking risk.
segments.catch: Match the size to the dog.

segments.name: Apple AirTag
segments.text: Number seventeen. An Apple AirTag, about twenty-three dollars. No more where-are-my-keys mornings. The catch? It's iPhone only. For Android, get a SmartTag or Tile.
segments.catch: iPhone only. Android? Get a SmartTag or Tile.

segments.name: Wearable sherpa blanket
segments.text: Number eighteen. A wearable sherpa blanket, about twenty-five dollars. The coziest gift on this whole list. The catch? It's one size and bulky, so it's a sofa thing.
segments.catch: One size and bulky. Sofa only.

segments.name: LEGO Botanicals Tiny Plants
segments.text: Number nineteen. LEGO Botanicals Tiny Plants, about forty dollars. A calm afternoon, and plants that never wilt. The catch? It takes a few hours, so it's best for someone who likes a project.
segments.catch: A few hours to build.

segments.name: Kindle Colorsoft
segments.text: And number twenty. The Kindle Colorsoft, about two hundred and ninety dollars. Cookbooks and comics in color, all in one bag. The catch? For plain novels, a regular Kindle costs less.
segments.catch: Novels only? A regular Kindle costs less.

segments.text: If you only buy one: the slippers she'll wear every night, the skillet that lasts a lifetime, or the AirTag that ends lost-key mornings.
Every pick is linked in the description, with the full guides for the US and the UK. Send this to someone with a long list. Happy holidays.
